page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1ne.6xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor operating at 2.5 GHz. The configuration provides 24 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 12 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with 192.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. No local storage or GPU accelerators are bundled with this instance type.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core performance, as measured by stress-ng and Geekbench, falls into the bottom 25%, reflecting the moderate 2.5 GHz clock speed of the older Intel Xeon architecture. However, multi-core benchmarks, including multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and Geekbench multi-core tests, reach average tiers. Memory bandwidth tests also show average performance, with read-only small block cached bandwidth at 984.37 GB/sec and uncached large block write bandwidth at 52.55 GB/sec.

The primary tradeoff of the ecs.se1ne.6xlarge is its reliance on network-attached storage, as it lacks local NVMe SSDs, and its baseline network bandwidth is limited to 4 Gbps. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the instance offers a dense memory allocation relative to its compute resources, making it a viable option for memory-bound workloads that do not demand high single-threaded CPU performance.

This hardware profile is suited for memory-intensive applications such as medium-sized databases, caching layers like Redis, enterprise applications, and memory-bound data processing tasks. It is also capable of handling static web serving and moderate multi-threaded compilation tasks.
